item: N12(vi) content review -- the finding retained in history (release v2, 2026-11-02; --retained-only)

scope.mode: --retained-only: each RETAINED entry's versions are read and checked (retained_in_history); a full run's scope is read for the et-al allowlist only, and nothing in it is screened or reported
scope.content_source: git objects via git cat-file --batch and git show (committed bytes; working tree not read)

method.line_split: on \n; 'lines' = number of \n-separated lines (a trailing newline does not add a line)
method.names: tier_a: capitalised word pairs, neither word in the name allowlist (counts only); tier_b: tier_a pairs whose first word is in the embedded given-name list (381 names; counts and line numbers only, never the names)

retained_in_history.rule: release v2 (2026-11-02): every run checks each entry against the git objects and exits without writing unless every check holds (checks); counts, line numbers and object ids only, never a name; each pair found joins the leak guard; nothing here is added to objects or totals

code_question.words_verbatim: Should a history rewrite remove the two names still in 908a659's blob?

pi_answer.words_verbatim: Keep history. Have the content screen’s raw record the finding exactly as it is — two third-party names in blob 908a659, removed from the tree at c2a6417, retained in history, with the reason (no private content; published co-authors of a cited paper) — so the scrub index carries the disposition rather than a reader discovering it.

entries.finding: 2 given-name pairs (tier b, 2 distinct), all on line 5 of the blob at 908a659 (the version that commit added); removed from the tree at c2a6417, which changed that line only and left no pair on it (none at --rev either); retained in history: 908a659 is an ancestor of --rev
entries.reason: no private content; published co-authors of a cited paper
entries.reason_from: the PI's answer of 2026-11-02 (pi_answer), its parenthesis, verbatim

leak_guard.rule: a full run's rule: every collected raw value of length >= 5 -- here the non-allowlisted identity names and e-mails of the commit and tag headers, the pairs found in each RETAINED version and any other value the screen collects from the versions it reads for retained_in_history -- asserted absent from the JSON text and the stdout summary before either is written; exempt: the two allowlisted e-mails, the allowlisted identity names, and standard OpenSSH file names ['authorized_keys', 'config', 'environment', 'known_hosts', 'known_hosts.old', 'rc']; the JSON is checked with the 'patterns' block and every 'method' entry except ['name_allowlist_et_al_detected', 'hex_tokens_skipped'] blanked
